correctness.rationale: The pre-step-refreshed state matrices yield the exact positive moment map \(\mathcal T(C)=\mathbb E[BCB^\top]\). For \(d=p+(1-p)h\), \(y=p(1-h)/d\), and \(P=\bigl(\begin{smallmatrix}1&y\\y&1\end{smallmatrix}\bigr)\), direct independent averaging gives \(\mathcal T^2(P)=P-(hQ/d)K\), with \(K=E+\mathcal T(E)\succ0\) and \(E=\operatorname{diag}(1,0)\). On \(0<h<2\), these strict positive-cone inequalities prove geometric contraction or expansion according to the sign of \(Q\), which has one positive root in \((0,2)\). From common nonzero initialization the covariance becomes positive definite by the third step. At \(h=2\) the same expansion identity applies; \(P\) is semidefinite only at \(p=1\), but the positive-cone comparison still proves growth. For \(h>2\), the mean explodes. Implicit differentiation of \(\partial_pQ=(h-1)(h-2)\) proves the exact monotonicity switch at \(v^2=1/2\). The enclosed standalone checker passed 1,710 exact rational cases plus the witness; finite computations do not replace the symbolic proof.

value.rationale: Snapshot-refresh probability is a controllable and computationally meaningful design parameter of loopless SVRG. The exact stable-step frontier has a strict, counterintuitive reversal: at small positive curvature contrast, more frequent refresh can render an otherwise convergent fixed-step algorithm divergent; at large contrast, the direction reverses. The concrete \(v=1/2\), \(h=5/4\) example gives opposite convergence classifications for two rational refresh probabilities. This does not claim a new \(p=1/2\) slice, arbitrary nonquadratic behavior, or practical speedup.
